reflexion_entries_to_archive.lesson: The 5.5-week dark outage was invisible because the ONLY crash signal was a >60s heartbeat-staleness check, and a fast restart always rewrites a fresh heartbeat before it fires. The real signal was hiding in plain sight: the heartbeat file is unlinked ONLY on graceful shutdown, so its PRESENCE at boot already means the prior run ended uncleanly, and its recorded `uptime` tells you how long that run survived. Short (<5min) unclean run x3 = crash-loop -> degraded in /health/deep. Detection lives BEFORE startHeartbeatFile() overwrites it. Corollary durability rule: a counter meant to detect torn-write crashes must itself tolerate a torn counter file (readJsonSafe->0), use atomicWriteFileSync, and be named so cleanupStaleTmps (reaps *.tmp-*) can't wipe it.

A shareable/downloadable artifact is a one-way information release â€” treat its inputs adversarially. Two gates made the Royal Summons safe to ship before the T3.1 anachronism filter exists: (1) a persona ALLOWLIST (known class, clamped rank, period-safe title charset) so a player-influenced/emergent field can't stamp a modern token on a hard-1601 image; (2) a DATE GATE (REAL_FESTIVAL_DATE=null â†’ 'proclaimed anon') so an unconfirmed placeholder year never propagates on an image people screenshot and share. Both were adversarial-challenge findings, not obvious from the happy path. Also: keeping the render 100% client-side (canvasâ†’PNG, reusing the shipped og-card pattern) delivered the funnel piece with zero new deps and zero infra â€” the cheapest possible first conversion step.

reflexion_entries_to_archive.lesson: The reveal flags were dead because two layers dropped them: resolveEmergentQuest flattens the standard-path reward to {deniers,reputation} in the caller, and the EmergentQuest instance never stores flags/title/chronicle at all (only rewardDeniers/rewardReputation survive instantiation). So the fix could NOT live in resolveEmergentQuest (no data there). The right seam was completeEmergentQuest, which already looks up the TEMPLATE â€” apply the missing reward TYPES from the EFFECTIVE reward (choice.rewards vs template.rewards) and split by ownership: flags -> quest-engine playerState (index.ts), title/chronicle -> gameState via applyReward. Crucially, leave deniers/reputation exactly as-is so a shared-path change doesn't shift economy. And the standard-only guard on title/chronicle avoids double-applying the choice path (which already forwards its full config). A focused real-path test on the actual B55 quest (not a mock) is what caught the immutable-addEntry drop.
reflexion_entries_to_archive.carry_forward: consequence-path chronicleEntry had the same immutable-addEntry drop; fixed in-pass + documented (behavior change: consequence chronicle entries now appear).

reflexion_entries_to_archive.lesson: chronicle.addEntry() returns a NEW ChronicleState and does not mutate its argument. Two call sites (reward + consequence) discarded the return, so EVERY quest-driven chronicle entry was silently lost â€” invisible because chronicle is narrative flavor nobody asserted on. Only a test asserting the entry APPEARS (count === expected) surfaced it. Rule: when a helper's signature returns state (functional/immutable style), grep every caller for `x = helper(x)` vs a bare `helper(x)` â€” a bare call on an immutable helper is almost always a dropped-write bug.

The rate-limit-collapse fix hinged on which header the proxy forwards, and the adversarial pass was right to make it a hard branch-gate: `trust proxy: true` is a security regression (spoofable), and `trust proxy: <hop>` silently fails if the proxy only sets CF-Connecting-IP and not XFF. Resolved by EMPIRICAL state-discovery (read .cloudflared/config.yml -> it's a Cloudflare Tunnel to 127.0.0.1) rather than guessing: that told me (a) trust ONLY loopback (the tunnel peer), never blanket true, and (b) CF-Connecting-IP is the authoritative, edge-overwritten, non-spoofable key. Belt-and-suspenders (trust proxy loopback for req.ip everywhere + CF-Connecting-IP key on the sensitive limiter) covers both header cases. Proved with a real-HTTP integration test whose key assertion (a different XFF must be a FRESH bucket) fails loudly if req.ip ever collapses to loopback again.

The adversarial pass caught a HIGH defect the synthesis rubber-stamped: the event-driven save for paid conversions was scoped to routes.ts / the /checkout POST, but the entitlement is only granted later in the Stripe WEBHOOK (ticket-routes.ts grantTicket, checkout.session.completed). A save at /checkout persists NOTHING â€” it would have been a fix that provably doesn't survive the crash it claims to prevent. Lesson: for 'save after high-value mutation', empirically trace WHERE the mutation actually lands (and that attachSidecarData() serializes it â€” _ticketState at :1203) before choosing the hook site. Also verified on a scratch-port throwaway killed before its 30s persist tick so the live parked save was never touched â€” test durability changes without gambling the production world.
